scope: Mounted driver/commander native command and fixed-path restoration assumptions

findings.finding: Its commentary reports that fixed paths could detach a separately commanded driver into DoNotPlan, and the commanded-vehicle restoration branch avoids waypoint recreation/fixed-path termination in favour of the current waypoint plus commander move. This is a preserved upstream observation, not verified CBE runtime evidence.

The navigation-area branch nevertheless approaches through effectiveCommander doMove, crosses with setDriveOnPath and calls refreshRoute on completion/timeout. No distinct-commander exclusion was found in this branch. Upstream methods are internally in tension; neither blanket support nor blanket failure follows from one helper comment.

findings.source: CBE current bypass/corridor return and DrivingRecoveryCommandState
findings.finding: CBE stops owned actors before fixed-path use, returns through commander move and requires both original-goal MOVE acknowledgements for temporary native return. A driver native destination planning mode does not by itself prove currentCommand or exact crew ACK transitions. Source-shaped tests do not settle whether this pattern is achievable on each vehicle/seat configuration.

officialReferences.supports: Owner-local destination array contains destination, planningMode and forceReplan; VEHICLE PLANNED is documented for vehicle driver. It does not specify the two-seat task transitions required by CBE.
Fixed-path driving is not established by unitReady; normal AI requires stop/detachment, and other movement/doStop cancels fixed-path effect. This does not prove later crew route restoration.
Native group formation can reassert after a unit finishes its move. The general command entry is not a guarantee of mounted two-seat acknowledgement behaviour.
